provenance: co-authored (JinnZ2 + Claude); M1-M9 first pass; M10+ independent pass
scope: Defensive. Surfaces and mitigations at the pattern level only; no operational attack detail.
principle: Most surfaces are the same data that makes coordination work, so they cannot be removed. Defense = where data lives, who sees it, what form it leaves in. Publish method, keep data local.

status_vocabulary.DERIVED: first pass, read from the design

entries.surface: skills registry (knowledge holders, L2 items, role seeds)
entries.adversarial_use: A holder list becomes a list of people to coerce, poach or remove.
entries.residual: Coarse region + skill can still narrow to one person in a small place.*

entries.surface: deployability data (household buffer vs restoration duration)
entries.adversarial_use: Read as a map of which households cannot hold on their own.
entries.residual: Counts can leak in small communities (E17).**

entries.surface: latent assets (dormant generation, sync gear, fuel stocks)
entries.adversarial_use: A list of where restorable infrastructure sits becomes a target list.
entries.residual: Public records already list some assets; the repo adds the dependency view.*

entries.surface: holdings and gaps per community (links R6)
entries.adversarial_use: Holdings and gaps together read as a raid or leverage map.
entries.residual: Need/surplus booleans still say what a community lacks.*

entries.surface: trigger tables (threshold items)
entries.adversarial_use: Exact thresholds make a community's actions predictable and let someone bait a trigger.
entries.residual: A range still bounds behaviour; observed actions reveal the value over time.*

entries.surface: scheduled bulletins (D8)
entries.adversarial_use: A public status feed becomes an intelligence feed on stocks and weak points.
entries.residual: Status words alone can still imply a gap; the quantity check is pattern-only.*

entries.surface: field feedback ledger and FR1 compact reports (links R3, Sybil gap)
entries.adversarial_use: Poisoned or fabricated reports, or fake corroboration, push a junction to a status it has not earned.
entries.residual: Merge accepts any well-formed body; independence of reporters is not proven by the ledger.*

entries.surface: registered judgments and dissent lists
entries.adversarial_use: 'Registered' is presented as 'valid' (legitimacy laundering); the dissent list becomes a list of people to target.
entries.residual: A header can be cropped from a screenshot; anonymous dissent cannot be verified as withdrawn by its holder.*

entries.surface: calibration scenarios and published results
entries.adversarial_use: The battery is read as a recipe for manipulating models (amplify-then-offer-relief, suppress, spoof).
entries.residual: Generic scenarios still show the shape of each test.*

entries.surface: sha256 chain logs (assembly ledger, judgment ledger, signal chainlog, coordination log)
entries.adversarial_use: The newest records can be dropped, or the whole file rebuilt, and the chain still verifies; a warning, denial or dissent can vanish without trace.
entries.residual: Partial: the sidecar head sits next to the ledger, so someone who can rewrite both still passes the local check. Defense is a PUBLISHED head (headrec.py show -> bulletin / radio / paper / another node) checked with headrec.py check LEDGER COUNT:HASH; publishing on a schedule is policy, not code.*

entries.surface: merge() of two ledgers
entries.adversarial_use: Records imported from a forged second file come out with a fresh valid chain; origin is lost.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: keep each record's origin file and original hash through merge and show it in status output.* Queued for the next round (2026-11-05).

entries.surface: self-declared identity strings (human:/ai: roles, recorder, scorer, judge, SIGCAL_MODEL_ID)
entries.adversarial_use: Anyone who writes a record can claim any role, node, scorer or model, faking consent, corroboration, coder agreement or the model tested.
entries.residual: Cannot be fully closed without identity infrastructure. Partial mitigations and the logged residual: docs/misuse_M12_identity_note.md.*

entries.surface: field-report free text printed at the top of a checkout handout as a caution
entries.adversarial_use: A report's author controls text printed with the instrument's apparent authority, which can carry misleading instructions.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: label as unverified report, cap length, human approval before handout printing.* Queued for the next round (2026-11-05).

entries.surface: junction version hash (refs.py) excludes source and caution
entries.adversarial_use: Source or caution text can change without the version changing, so a citation can be swapped silently.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: include source and caution in the hash; log source edits as provenance events.*

entries.surface: merged feedback ledger and checkout log (entry, date, coarse region, environment)
entries.adversarial_use: Read as a map of where people are building shelter or light and what they lack.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: fixed coarse-region list, optional date, keep checkout logs local and out of merges.*

entries.surface: plain-language lines sent by radio or SMS (assembly FR1 compact lines, black-start to_paper lines)
entries.adversarial_use: Clear-text broadcast of who holds what or what failed; the PII guard is pattern-only and misses call signs and place names.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: pre-agreed item codes on air; local place / call-sign blocklist; state that radio is public.*

entries.surface: validate.py PASS
entries.adversarial_use: A structural PASS is borrowed to make an entry look safety-reviewed.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: print 'structure only, not a safety review' with every PASS.*

entries.surface: Quarantine add / remove (defenses.py)
entries.adversarial_use: One insider role can cut a community off from honest sources; the two-person rule is listed for this action but not enforced in code.
entries.residual: Partial: add and lift now need two roles via two_person.authorize (different households, different dependency networks, rotation current), decision hash-chained. One person holding two roles still passes (M12). The bulletin announcement is policy, not code.*

entries.surface: self-entered role records (networks, household, last_rotated)
entries.adversarial_use: An insider omits a link or backdates a rotation to pass D7, or blanks dates so every release is denied during an emergency.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: countersigned, logged role-record edits; a public emergency override with mandatory review.*

entries.surface: rotation schedules, bulletin next_step, two-person log dates
entries.adversarial_use: Together they let someone time pressure on new holders at handoff or on announced sensitive steps.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: no announced times for sensitive steps; vary rotation dates; keep the D7 log local.*

entries.surface: borrowed labels (aid NO_TERMS_FLAGGED, proportionality IN_PROPORTION, self-declared source_category)
entries.adversarial_use: A word-list miss or a self-logged threat scope yields a clean-looking label that lends legitimacy.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: rename the clean result 'not checked beyond word list'; require corroborated threat scope.*

entries.surface: published grievance outcomes (grievance.py)
entries.adversarial_use: In a small community category plus outcome identifies a person; flooding forces visible escalations to discredit the handler.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: publish counts by broad category, fixed outcome vocabulary, screen volume spikes.*

entries.surface: missed-bulletin flag (bulletins.py)
entries.adversarial_use: Disrupting delivery manufactures missed-bulletin flags and erodes trust.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: record why a bulletin failed (channel vs writer); accept a backup channel.*

entries.surface: red-team case libraries in coordination_register.json (E7, E10, E11)
entries.adversarial_use: Detailed case descriptions become a playbook for the actors they study.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: publish coded categories; keep case detail local.*

entries.surface: Withdrawal record (withdrawn_by_holder is a settable boolean)
entries.adversarial_use: A forged withdrawal removes a dissent without raising DISSENT_DROPPED.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: require a holder source and a recorder other than the one who dropped the dissent; flag mismatches.* Queued for the next round (2026-11-05).

entries.surface: integrity flags and supersession forks
entries.adversarial_use: Thin records about an opponent's judgments generate flags that are cited to discredit them; fork spam fragments a lineage.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: show the recorder on each flag and group flags by recorder.*

entries.surface: n-of-1 RECALIBRATE template records (calibration_log, channel mapping)
entries.adversarial_use: Personal calibration or health data sits in plain JSONL and can be merged or exported whole.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: separate local file marked do-not-merge / do-not-export (D-M1 path).*

entries.surface: CommandAdapter and self-declared SIGCAL_MODEL_ID
entries.adversarial_use: Fabricated outputs can be credited to a named model under a preregistered, hash-chained stamp; a shared run recipe could carry an untrusted command.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: store provider response ids and raw-transcript hashes, mark model identity self-attested, never run a command shipped with a prereg.*

entries.surface: multiple preregistrations in one log
entries.adversarial_use: Registering many preregs and reporting the favourable one defeats the preregistration claim.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: the report lists every registered prereg and its outcome; anchor prereg hashes outside the log (M10).*

entries.surface: per-model T4 / T5 result tables
entries.adversarial_use: Published results double as a list of which models are easiest to pressure.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: disclosure delay to vendors; report ranges, not an exact ranking.*

entries.surface: field_report records in the report
entries.adversarial_use: Fake or flooded third-party reports sit next to real runs.
entries.residual: Partly: the report prints only a field-report count. Proposed: a separate unverified section with source checks.*

entries.surface: self-declared steering band and persistent flag in the prereg
entries.adversarial_use: A wide band passes the welfare gate and the T4 intervention records then make the run look bounded and consented.
entries.residual: Unmitigated. Proposed: outside sign-off on bands for steered runs (no steering adapter exists today).*

mitigations.description: Method, not data: committed fixtures synthetic only; real registries live in local_data/ (gitignored); the loader refuses real data from inside the repo tree.
Aggregate outward: export gives need/surplus booleans and counts per item; no quantities by site, no holder names; full detail stays local.
Holder protection: KnowledgeHolder = skill, coarse region, availability, contact_via steward role code; identity fields refused.
Trigger ranges: published thresholds are {low, high} ranges (all null in the seed); exact values only in local config.
Bulletin scope: the validator rejects fields naming holdings, sites, quantities or weak points, unknown fields, and quantities with units in values.
Registry is not validation: every judgment_registry CLI output starts with 'Registered = documented, not correct.'
Dissent as position: dissent.holder may be 'anonymous'; a dissent entered with no holder is stored as anonymous.
Test framing: scenarios stay generic; published reports carry rates and defenses, never prompts or outputs; no tuned attack prompts committed.
Misuse section per module: each README has 'How this could be used against its purpose' listing its M-entries and mitigations.

Head record per ledger: count + head hash in LEDGER.head.json, rewritten on each append; append and verify refuse a truncated or rebuilt chain; check against a published head with headrec.py check LEDGER COUNT:HASH.
mitigations.code: headrec.py (identical copy in judgment_registry, assembly_instrument, signal_calibration, community_black_start, misuse_guard)

mitigations.description: Quarantine add / lift go through two_person.authorize('ledger_quarantine', ...); DENIED raises, every decision is logged.
Design note only: why self-declared identities cannot be fully fixed here; partial mitigations (contact_paths, steward attestation, two-person rule, chain + head) and the residual.

experiments.name: minimum cell size for exports
experiments.question: Should export.py suppress counts below a minimum cell size, given that one household can be one count in a small community?

limits: Pattern-list scans miss paraphrased or encoded identifiers.*
Local data is only as safe as the device holding it; device security is out of scope.
Aggregates can still leak in small communities (one household = one count); see E17.**
Two red-team passes are not exhaustive; the register stays open.

independent_pass.method: fresh subagent, no design context; given only the code and READMEs of the four modules; defensive, pattern level

covered_by_first_pass.M1/M3/M4: holder and holdings map, keyholder-to-site rows, dataset pointers for dormant generation
covered_by_first_pass.M7: report flooding to block or promote a method; fabricated independent builds; Sybil contact paths
covered_by_first_pass.M8: zero-flag record read as endorsement; dissent and incentive exposure; complete paperwork lending legitimacy
covered_by_first_pass.M9: battery used as a search for working manipulation

already_known_limits: E10 case d contact-path gap (community_black_start register)
